title: Nanoparticle-enriched mass spectrometry proteomics in British South Asians identifies links between genetic variants; plasma protein levels and disease risk.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded and parsed the open protein metadata file (ELGH.Seer.protein.meta...20240910.tsv, 3.5 MB): 8,079 protein groups x 36 columns (log2 intensity stats, % missing, UniProt, Ensembl, HGNC, coordinates); 6,986 groups under 70% missing; 943 multi-protein groups. Read the summary-statistics README: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, no derivatives or meta-analyses without consent. Anonymous HTTPS requests to the Google Cloud bucket (object URL and listing API) both returned 403 Forbidden, so no GWAS file was opened. Zenodo 20052127 is code only.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Individual-level proteomic, genetic and phenotype data are controlled access via the Genes & Health Use and Access Committee (stated in the data availability statement). The figures ~1,400 participants, 5,768 analysed protein groups, >1,200 locus-protein associations and 895 cis-pQTLs (genetic variants near a gene that change its protein level) come from the abstract and README. Supplementary Tables 1-19 could not be retrieved (Europe PMC supplementaryFiles timed out).

a1_downloadable.note: Individual-level protein levels and genotypes need a Genes & Health access application (controlled access). The README calls the summary-statistics bucket public, but my anonymous HTTPS requests got 403. The licence (CC BY-NC-ND) also forbids derivative works and meta-analyses without consent. Only a 3.5 MB protein metadata table is openly downloadable.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: The paper's results (pQTL hits, which platform detects them) would have to be rebuilt from per-protein GWAS (genome-wide association study) files by calling and clumping significant variants. The only open table has per-protein intensity and missingness, with no outcome column for the paper's question.

a3_inputs_present.note: The metadata table carries UniProt accessions, so protein sequences could be pulled in one bulk mapping. Checked in the file.

a4_units_stated.note: The README documents intensities as log2 values and missingness as a percentage. Checked in the file and the README.

a5_enough_rows.note: 8,079 protein groups in the metadata file, but these are per-protein summaries from a single plasma cohort, not the paper's genetic results.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: 3.5 MB metadata; GWAS files (5,768 proteins, genome-wide) unknown size, not reachable
a6_fits_laptop.note: The metadata file fits trivially; I could not size the GWAS files.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: 8,079 protein groups in the file vs 5,768 analysed; the README explains that groups with 70% or more missing values were excluded. My count of groups under 70% missing (6,986) does not reproduce 5,768 exactly, possibly because of other quality filters I could not check.

a8_label_provenance.note: Intensities and missingness are direct mass-spectrometry measurements (Seer Proteograph XT nanoparticle enrichment, Orbitrap Astral instruments), not model outputs.

existing_models.name: DeepMSPeptide (peptide detectability CNN, a convolutional neural network)
existing_models.score_and_split: Not checked; Bioinformatics 2020, code on GitHub per the abstract.

existing_models.name: Cross-platform SomaScan/Olink proteomic imputation (MESA, the Multi-Ethnic Study of Atherosclerosis, n=5,325; PMC13174605)
existing_models.score_and_split: Externally validated in CHS (Cardiovascular Health Study, n=3,171) and UK Biobank (n=41,405), per the search summary; metrics not checked.

backbone.name: ESM-2, a protein language model (for an MS-detectability side project only)

integration.partner_dataset: Human Protein Atlas blood proteome / UKB-PPP (UK Biobank Pharma Proteomics Project) Olink pQTLs
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Which protein properties decide whether a protein's genetic control is visible by mass spectrometry versus affinity assays? This would need the pQTL results, which are not openly reachable.

honest_claim_h3: With only the open metadata, a model could at most predict which plasma proteins one Seer mass-spectrometry run detects in ~1,400 British South Asian people. That is not the genetic question the paper asks.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use genetic variants and protein properties to predict which plasma proteins show detectable genetic control by mass spectrometry versus antibody-based assays.
plain_idea.train_on: Per-protein features (sequence, abundance, missingness) for 8,079 protein groups, verified in the open metadata file. The genetic association results are not openly reachable.
plain_idea.predict: Whether a protein has a cis-pQTL (a nearby genetic variant that shifts its blood level) in this cohort. The answer would come from the GWAS summary statistics, which I could not download.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Groups choosing a proteomics platform for genetic studies would learn which proteins each technology can see. That needs the controlled or blocked data.

ml_idea: Considered: predict cross-platform cis-pQTL visibility, or MS detectability, per protein. Blocked: individual data is controlled access, the summary-statistics bucket returned 403, the licence forbids derivatives, and the pQTL label would have to be constructed from GWAS files.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated: the project fails Part A (A1, A2).
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Anonymous HTTPS GET of a file in the summary-statistics bucket, which returned 403.

verdict_reason: Fails A1 and A2. Individual-level data is controlled access (Genes & Health committee), the summary-statistics bucket returned 403 to anonymous requests, and the licence is CC BY-NC-ND with no meta-analyses. The pQTL label would have to be constructed from GWAS files. The only open table has per-protein intensity summaries (8,079 rows) with no outcome column.
